biography:
I am in Energy and Infrastructure, Global Data Centers at Google with over 10 years of professional experience and I hold a Master’s degree from Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS) with concentrations in International Economics and Energy, Resources, and Environment. I optimize 24/7 clean energy procurement, energy transition to low-carbon and carbon-free sources, and enhance resiliency and sustainability. My areas of expertise include utilities' business models, electricity markets, regulatory frameworks, energy infrastructure, third party financed projects, distributed energy resources, electricity access in rural areas, oil and natural gas markets, nuclear industry and uranium market and small modular reactors, hydrogen, solar and wind technologies deployment, electric vehicles and charging infrastructure, smart meters, battery energy storage, metals commodities, critical minerals/rare earth elements/battery metals mining recycling and reuse, ESG, data center infrastructure, financial analysis, risk analysis, and dam management. I am passionate about solving energy challenges, creating value for stakeholders and society, fascinated with energy markets focusing on developers, regulatory, and business model components and am interested in international development, trade, and diplomacy.

I am an International Affairs and Policy Specialist, having lived in the Former Soviet Union for 11 years - in Ukraine, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan, where I learned Russian, Uzbek, and Tajik and worked on social entrepreneurial and humanitarian aid projects. I spent one year 2014-2015 working in Ukraine during civil unrest and war with Transparency International in Kyiv and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees in Donetsk. I graduated from the University of Virginia Frank Batten School of Leadership & Public Policy with two Bachelor’s degrees in Leadership & Public Policy and in Foreign Affairs with concentrations on Europe, Asia, and Africa.

My experience includes tech industry, consulting, U.S. federal government, think tanks, and international organizations that deal with energy (electricity, renewable sources, energy battery storage, natural gas, nuclear, electric vehicles), resources (food, water, land use, critical minerals/rare earth elements/battery metals), human rights and rule of law (conflict management and resolution, refugees and resettlement), international relations and international development (Russia, Eastern Europe, Central Asia, Eurasia, Japan, Korea, China).

I speak Russian, Uzbek, and Tajik.
